''Siyah Beyazlılar'' ({{Literal translation|Black and Whites}}) | short name = BJK | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|1903|3|3}}
as ''Bereket Jimnastik Kulübü''{{cite web |url=https://bjk.com.tr/tr/cms/tarihce/2/73 |title=Kulüp Tarihçesi |website=Beşiktaş JK |publisher=Beşiktaş Jimnastik Kulübü |language=tr |access-date=9 August 2025}} | ground = [[Beşiktaş Stadıum]], [[Beşiktaş]], [[Istanbul]] | capacity = 42,684 | coordinates = {{Coord|41.039167|28.994722|format=dms|type:landmark_scale:3000_region:TR|display=it}} | chrtitle = President | chairman = Serdal Adalı | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Vincenzo Italiano]] | league = {{Turkish football updater|Beşiktaş}} | season = {{Turkish football updater|Beşiktaş2}} | position = {{Turkish football updater|Beşiktaş3}} | website = {{URL|https://www.bjk.com.tr/|bjk.com.tr}} | pattern_la1 = _besiktas2627h | pattern_b1 = _besiktas2627h | pattern_ra1 = _besiktas2627h | pattern_sh1 = _nikeleague3b | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = ffffff | body1 = ffffff | rightarm1 = ffffff | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = ffffff | pattern_la2 = _besiktas2627h | pattern_b2 = _besiktas2627a | pattern_ra2 = _besiktas2627h | pattern_sh2 = _nikeleague3wb | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = | body2 = | rightarm2 = | shorts2 = | socks2 = 000000 | pattern_la3 = _besiktas2627t | pattern_b3 = _besiktas2627t | pattern_ra3 = _besiktas2627t | pattern_sh3 = _besiktas2627t | pattern_so3 = | shorts3 = ffffff | socks3 = 000000 | stadium = [[Beşiktaş Stadium]] }} {{Beşiktaş J.K. sections}} '''Beşiktaş Jimnastik Kulübü''' ({{IPA|tr|beˈʃictaʃ}}, {{Literal translation|Beşiktaş Gymnastics Club}}), abbreviated as '''BJK''', is a Turkish professional [[sports club]] founded in 1903 that is based in the [[Beşiktaş]] district, [[Istanbul]]. The club's football team is one of the [[Big Three (Turkey)|Big Three]] in [[Turkey]] and one of the most successful teams in the country, having never been relegated to a lower division. It was the first registered sports club in the country and one of the few that acquired the right to bear the [[Flag of Turkey|Turkish flag]] on its crest. Its football team has won 21 league titles including 16 [[Süper Lig|Turkish Süper Lig]], three [[Turkish National Division]] and two [[Turkish Football Championship]] titles, along with 11 [[Turkish Cup]] titles. Beşiktaş is also the only team to have won the Süper Lig undefeated, in the [[1991–92 1.Lig|1991–92 campaign]]. The team last won the Turkish [[Süper Lig]] title during the [[2020–21 Süper Lig|2020–21 season]] and the Turkish Cup in the [[2023–24 Süper Lig|2023–24 season]]. The club's home ground is [[Beşiktaş Stadium]], a 42,684-capacity [[all-seater stadium]] located by [[Dolmabahçe Palace]]. The stadium has been considered one of the best in the world for location, design, comfort, technology, atmosphere, and transportation.{{cite news |title=Vodafone Park wins Stadium Project of the Year |url=https://turkish-football.com/liverpool-fc-las-vegas-project-pipped-by-the-besiktas-vodafone-park-for-stadium-project-of-the-year-award/ |access-date=9 August 2025 |work=Turkish-Football.com |publisher=Turkish Football |language=en}} The team also participates in European competitions regularly. Beşiktaş reached the quarter-finals of the [[1986–87 European Cup]] and displayed the best Turkish team performance in the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] group stage by earning 14 points and progressing undefeated in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|2017–18]] campaign. Beşiktaş have also reached the [[UEFA Europa League]]{{efn|Known as [[UEFA Cup]] until [[2008–09 UEFA Cup|2008–09 season]].}} quarter-finals twice, in the [[2002–03 UEFA Cup|2002–03]] and [[2016–17 UEFA Europa League|2016–17]] seasons. Based on its [[UEFA coefficient]], Beşiktaş is currently the 4th highest ranked Turkish team and is ranked third all-time after its rivals [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] and [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]].{{Cite web |title=Club coefficients: UEFA rankings |url=https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/uefarankings/club/?year=2026 |access-date=2024-04-17 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}} The club's fan base, [[Çarşı (supporter group)|Çarşı]], is well known globally.{{cite magazine |last=Batuman |first=Elif |date=7 March 2011 |title=The View from the Stands |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2011/03/07/the-view-from-the-stands |access-date=9 August 2025 |department=Letter from Turkey |magazine=The New Yorker |language=en}} They were chosen as the best fan group in voting conducted by American sports viewers due to their 132-decibel noise record at a 2007 match against [[Liverpool FC|Liverpool]].{{cite web |title=What makes round of 16 debutants Beşiktaş special? |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5116bc76b4-25dec61dbf40-1000--what-makes-round-of-16-debutants-besiktas-special/ |access-date=9 August 2025 |website=UEFA |language=en}} The group is involved with sociopolitical causes and is traditionally considered to be working-class and left-wing, supporting what is known as "the people's team".{{Cite news|last=McManus|first=John|date=2009-11-24|title=Besiktas fans reveal united front|language=en-GB|publisher=BBC|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8376619.stm|access-date=2021-06-27}} The highest ever football attendance in Turkish league history was recorded in a [[Beşiktaş–Galatasaray rivalry|Beşiktaş–Galatasaray derby]] with 76,127 spectators.{{cite news |title=Atatürk Olimpiyat Stadı'nda seyirci rekoru |url=https://www.sozcu.com.tr/ataturk-olimpiyat-stadinda-seyirci-rekoru-wp376377 |access-date=9 August 2025 |work=Sözcü |language=tr}}{{cite news |title=Beşiktaş–Galatasaray derbisinde 76 bin 127 seyirci |url=https://www.milliyet.com.tr/skorer/besiktas-galatasaray-derbisinde-76-bin-127-seyirci-2564835 |access-date=9 August 2025 |work=Milliyet |language=tr}} The club also competes in other sports such as [[Beşiktaş J.K. (women's football)|women's football]], basketball ([[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|men's]], [[Beşiktaş JK (women's basketball)|women's]] and [[Beşiktaş JK (wheelchair basketball)|wheelchair]]), volleyball ([[Beşiktaş JK (men's volleyball)|men's]] and [[Beşiktaş JK (women's volleyball)|women's]]), [[Beşiktaş JK (handball)|handball]], [[Beşiktaş J.K. (athletics)|athletics]], beach football, boxing, bridge, chess, gymnastics, athletics, parasports, rowing, table tennis, wrestling and [[esports]].{{cite web |title=Hakkında |url=https://bjk.com.tr/tr/cms/hakkinda/1/ |access-date=9 August 2025 |website=Beşiktaş JK |publisher=Beşiktaş Jimnastik Kulübü |language=tr}}"}}
